newsitem.title: JAPAN: INTERVIEW - NCB to keep raising funds by debentures.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - NCB to keep raising funds by debentures.

text.p: The Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) said on Tuesday it believes it can continue to raise funds by issuing bank debentures for the time being, though it acknowledges some investors are being hit with losses.
NCB's outstanding bank debentures totalled about 9.59 trillion yen as of end-March 1996, a spokesman for the bank told Reuters in an interview.
The bank will have no problems in funding as long as the deviation between the market yield of NCB's debentures and its coupon rate is rectified at some point in the future, he added.
"If the current situation prevails year after year, we would be worried," he said. "But right now it is not a problem."
NCB's debentures should be attractive for investors who wish to hold on to the bonds until maturity, because the coupon rate is high compared to others, the spokesman said.
But the bank is concerned about the fact investors who purchase NCB's debentures on an underwriting basis are hit immediately with unrealised losses, he said.

"I think we are putting investors in a difficult situation," he said. "We would like to rectify the situation in which losses are incurred (by investors) as soon as they buy (the debentures), as soon as possible."

The NCB spokesman said current market conditions were "abnormal" and said he hoped that the spread between the market yields of NCB's debentures and the benchmark issued by the Industrial Bank of Japan would narrow in the future.
The official said, however, that the bank debenture market had calmed down since early February, when NCB's January debenture with a coupon rate of 2.15 percent was traded at 4.10 percent.

On Tuesday, there were neither offers nor bids for NCB's February five-year bank debentures with a coupon rate of 2.35 percent, traders said, but they said judging from current market conditions, the yield is likely to stand at somewhere above four percent.
In comparison, IBJ's February debentures with a coupon rate of 1.6 percent were offered at 1.67 percent.
The spokesman dismissed rumours that the Finance Ministry's (MOF) Trust Fund Bureau may have been purchasing NCB debentures in disproportionately large amounts since last year.
Rumours have swirled in the bond market recently that the Trust Fund Bureau had increased its purchases of NCB debentures in order to prevent prices from falling further.
Earlier this month, Nippon Credit's share prices fell on rumours that it was on the verge of collapse, and NCB vice president Shoji Nishikawa held a news conference to deny the rumours.

"In the markets, unsourced rumours such as the suggestion that our bank is practically on the verge of collapse are circulating and are prompting sales of our shares and debentures," Nishikawa told reporters.
Later, shares recovered partly on a comment by ruling party politician Taku Yamasaki that Nippon Credit's creditors holding the bank's debentures could be protected under various public funds.
NCB's problem loans totalled about 1.36 trillion yen, or 13.5 percent of the bank's outstanding loans, as of the end of September 1996.
NCB shares closed at 240 yen on Tuesday after plunging to a record low of 177 yen earlier this month. This compares with its all-time high of 19,400 yen set in December 1989.
